bull.b: A predominantly recurring revenue model improves visibility, supports customer lifetime expansion and reduces reliance on one-time sales. The subscription structure also lets revenue scale with usage, channels and enterprise adoption over time.

Accelerating revenue, 110% net retention and expanding large-account cohorts indicate strong product value and land-and-expand potential. Rising RPO provides multi-period visibility and supports continued growth as enterprise deployments deepen.

Positive operating and free cash flow despite reported losses demonstrates improving financial discipline and cash conversion. Low leverage preserves flexibility to invest in product development, enterprise growth and AI capabilities without substantial balance-sheet strain.

bear.b: Braze has not yet reached sustainable GAAP earnings, and the sharp deceleration from prior growth rates raises execution risk. Continued losses could limit internal reinvestment capacity and make future profitability dependent on renewed growth and operating leverage.

Premium messaging and carrier costs can structurally increase delivery expense as usage grows, while AI product staffing adds cost during scale-up. If pricing and productivity do not offset these pressures, incremental revenue may produce weaker long-term margin expansion.

Braze is scaling delivery, sales and product operations while resolving earlier Decisioning Studio capacity constraints. A CFO transition during this expansion adds oversight and execution risk, potentially delaying operating improvements or enterprise implementation momentum.
